title: Beta rollout plan + feature flagging for Route-level A/B testing (Console + routing)
creator: Dylan Brooks
body:
Objective
- Define and implement the staged beta rollout for Route-level A/B testing (Console-first) across regions and tiers (Hosted + Dedicated), using feature flags/entitlements.
- Ensure safe operational posture: monitoring checklist, guardrail alerts, and crisp rollback triggers/runbook linkage.

Scope
1) Feature flags / gating
- Add an entitlement/flag that gates:
  a) Console UI visibility (nav + create flow + results views)
  b) Control-plane APIs for experiment CRUD/start/stop
  c) Data-plane (gateway/routing) execution of experiment assignment
  d) Results aggregation queries (avoid expensive queries for non-enabled tenants)

- Proposed flags (names are placeholders; final names should match config-service conventions):
  - console.ab_testing_route_level_ui (Console UI)
  - controlplane.ab_experiments_enabled (CRUD/start/stop)
  - dataplane.route_ab_assignment_enabled (routing decision + exposure events)
  - telemetry.ab_exposure_ingest_enabled (ingestion switch; should stay on broadly once safe)

- Gating rules
  - Hosted: enabled by allowlist at org_id/project_id (beta partners + internal dogfood)
  - Dedicated: enabled by allowlist at deployment_id + org_id (avoid partial enablement inside a dedicated pool unless explicitly requested)
  - Private: OFF for beta (follow-on gating path; requires separate release vehicle)

2) Region rollout plan
- Regions targeted for beta
  - Phase A: us-east-1 (internal + 1 design partner)
  - Phase B: us-west-2 (add 1–2 partners; validate multi-region dashboards)
  - Phase C: eu-west-1 (only after confirming 429/guardrail behavior and capacity headroom; requires SRE sign-off)

- Rollout sequencing constraints
  - Telemetry pipeline changes must land and be stable before enabling Console results.
  - Exposure event tags must be in the reduced allowlist (avoid cardinality blowups). See ENG-2842 / PR-18519.
  - Guardrail evaluator + alert routing must be ready before enabling >10% traffic splits for any partner.

3) Beta enablement stages
- Stage 0: Dev/staging
  - Enable flags in staging for engineering QA + design review.
  - Confirm audit log events fire for create/update/start/stop/rollback.

- Stage 1: Internal dogfood (production, Redwood orgs only)
  - Allowlist internal orgs/projects (Console team + routing team).
  - Cap max split to 10% to variant B by validation rule in control-plane.
  - Require that assignments are stable across retries/stream reconnect (verify post PR-18504).

- Stage 2: Design partners (Hosted)
  - Allowlist 2–3 partners (tracked separately by PM; do not embed customer names here beyond internal code names).
  - Default max split 25% without SRE waiver.
  - Results dashboard available, but add UI copy that quality metrics may be incomplete unless eval suite attached.

- Stage 3: Design partners (Dedicated)
  - Only after we verify cost attribution by variant is correct and dashboards align with metering.
  - Require explicit capacity confirmation from Dedicated ops.

- Stage 4: Wider beta (self-serve request)
  - Request-based enablement via Support/CS workflow.
  - Add a lightweight checklist for Support to confirm region + route eligibility.

Monitoring checklist (must be completed before enabling Stage 2)
- Telemetry / data correctness
  - Exposure events present with expected sampling rate (by region) and stable schema version.
  - Variant distribution matches configured split within tolerance (±2% absolute for >50k exposures; looser for small samples).
  - Cost attribution for tokens/GPU includes experiment_id + variant_id and matches billing aggregates within acceptable drift.

- Performance & reliability
  - p95 latency and TTFT by variant and overall route within guardrails.
  - Error rate (5xx) and timeout rate do not regress beyond thresholds.
  - 429 rate monitored per region (explicitly called out due to prior staging incident and the eu-west constraint).
  - Verify fallback precedence behavior when variant capacity is constrained (experiment should not override safety fallbacks; see ADR-0187).

- Cardinality & cost of observability
  - Confirm metric tag allowlist enforcement is active.
  - Validate no unbounded dimensions (route template vs raw path; no request_id, no user_id).

- Operational readiness
  - Guardrail alerts are wired to on-call (SRE) + owning eng channel.
  - Runbook reviewed: confluence runbook “A/B testing emergency disable and rollback”.
  - Audit log export available to Security for beta partners who request it.

Rollback triggers (automatic + manual)
- Automatic rollback triggers (guardrail evaluator)
  - Any region: 5xx rate increase > 0.5% absolute for 10 minutes on the experimented route.
  - Any region: p95 latency regression > 15% for 10 minutes (overall route, not just variant B).
  - Any region: 429 rate > 1% for 5 minutes OR sustained elevated 429s compared to 7-day baseline.
  - Any region: exposure logging ingestion errors > 2% (pipeline failing may indicate instrumentation regression; we should fail open for routing but stop showing results).

- Manual rollback triggers
  - Partner reports correctness issues (variant flip, misrouting, unexpected model version) and we cannot reproduce quickly.
  - Console results mismatch with customer’s dashboard after confirming time window + sampling (route-level reporting integrity issue).

Rollback mechanisms
- Tier 1: disable dataplane.route_ab_assignment_enabled for org/project (immediately stops splitting; all traffic goes to control).
- Tier 2: stop experiment via control-plane API (clean lifecycle event + audit log).
- Tier 3: region-level kill switch for dataplane.route_ab_assignment_enabled (SRE only; for widespread incident).

Acceptance criteria
- Flags exist and are enforced at:
  - Console UI, control-plane APIs, and data-plane routing.
- Allowlist management documented (who can enable; how; audit trail).
- Region staging plan documented with explicit prerequisites and owner sign-offs.
- Monitoring checklist captured in a runbook / release checklist and linked from PM-481.
- Rollback triggers match SRE requirements and are implemented/confirmed in alert rules (ENG-2845).

Notes / references
- PM-481: GA/beta criteria alignment
- ENG-2845: dashboards + alert rules
- ENG-2842: exposure schema + ingestion
- ENG-2847: security review of permissions + audit events
- Release train coordination: eng-releases thread (internal)

Open questions
1) Should we enable telemetry.ab_exposure_ingest_enabled globally by default once safe, even if feature is gated? (Preferred: yes, but keep strict tag allowlist + sampling so we can debug and validate without UI exposure.)
2) Do we need a separate flag for results UI vs create/start UI? (Potentially yes to allow safe read-only preview.)
3) Dedicated gating: do we support enablement per route within a Dedicated deployment without a platform restart? (Assumption: yes via config propagation, but confirm propagation latencies and failure modes.)
comments: 2026-02-10 (Sean Gallagher): Before any external beta, we need explicit rollback triggers + alert routing. Please include 429 thresholds per region; eu-west has less headroom and tends to be noisier under burst.
2026-02-12 (Allison Grant): Please ensure tag allowlist enforcement is a hard gate. We’ve been burned by route-level labels before (raw path). Use route template / route_id only.

2026-02-14 (Chloe Martin): Console gating needs to cover both nav + deep links. We’ve had users discover hidden pages via direct URL; make the backend return 404/feature-disabled for non-entitled orgs.

2026-02-18 (Connor O'Brien): Drafted rollout stages. Need final sign-off on automatic rollback thresholds after ENG-2845 alert rules are finalized. Also aligning with release train sequencing: telemetry pipeline first, then Console results.

2026-02-22 (Marissa Cole): For beta partners, we should default to 90/10 or 75/25 splits and require a warning modal for 50/50. Include copy that guardrails may auto-rollback and that results may lag by aggregation window.
